body:
a woman half-submerged in a bathtub, in a diamond-lined bodysuit, under an orange glittering title. that is the cover of her twelfth album, the life of a showgirl — and it is a painting you have seen before.

mert alas and marcus piggott shot it as a restaging of millais's "ophelia," the 1851 painting of shakespeare's drowned girl. taylor kept the framing deliberately offstage: "my day ends in a bathtub, not usually in a bedazzled dress." she wanted the artwork to be about what happened away from the tour's spectacle, not on it.

and then the cover pays itself off. the ophelia floating there is the same woman track one goes and pulls back out of the water — the album opens by rescuing her.

her newest era has its own page on the site now. scrub over to it.

longlivets.com/?era=tloas&utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=era-deep-cut
